title: BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook: code allows ratio == 50 while NatSpec promises 'strictly < MAX_RATIO'
description: The hook's NatSpec declares: 'Exclusive upper bound on `ratio`. Max settable ratio is `MAX_RATIO - 1`' and 'Percentage of dispatched USDS that becomes debt. Strictly `< MAX_RATIO`.' The constructor and setter, however, allow ratio == MAX_RATIO (== 50): the check is `if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert RatioTooHigh()` (strictly greater than, not greater-or-equal), and DEFAULT_RATIO = 50 is assigned in the constructor without going through any guard. So the actual maximum settable ratio is 50, not 49 as the NatSpec promises. While 50% is not a security failure per se, the discrepancy is a spec violation that affects any external integrator relying on the documented invariant (e.g., a UI computing maximum possible debt accrual, an auditor verifying a 'cannot exceed 49%' guarantee). At 50%, the hook accrues mintDebt equal to half of every dispatched USDS amount — meaningful real-world consequence given pull() mints phUSD 1:1 to the recipient.
exploit_path:
1. Owner reads NatSpec and assumes ratio is capped at 49 (since 'strictly < 50').
2. Owner deploys hook; constructor sets ratio = DEFAULT_RATIO = 50 immediately. The hook is already running at the boundary of the documented invariant.
3. Later, owner can also setRatio(50) explicitly — the > check does not block it. Any downstream contract or off-chain monitor that assumes 'ratio < 50 enforced on-chain' is wrong.

No direct theft vector, but the on-chain reality diverges from the published spec, which could lead an integrator to skip a safety check they would otherwise have added.
mainnet_realism_check: Pure code/docs discrepancy. No external contract behaviour assumed.
recommendation: Either tighten the check to `if (newRatio >= MAX_RATIO) revert RatioTooHigh()` and lower DEFAULT_RATIO to 49 (matching the NatSpec), or update the NatSpec to say 'inclusive — max settable is MAX_RATIO'. Pick one. As written the contract and the comment disagree.
merge_rationale: Duplicate of ECON-RAW-008 (same contract, same lines, same off-by-one between docstring and `>` check, same severity). ECON-RAW-008 retained because it covers all the same content plus the cross-reference to ECON-RAW-003's debt-vs-realisable-USDC boundary case, giving better economic framing.
